Subject: Deployment mode follow-up — hosted vs dedicated vs private (noisy neighbor concerns)

Hi Samir / Lina —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we can map you to the right deployment mode (Hosted API vs Dedicated capacity vs Private VPC):

Summary of your needs
- High throughput across peak shopping events (blackout windows matter)
- Strong isolation guarantees for customer PII and payment anomalies buckets
- Predictable latency SLOs (p95 < 200ms for gen requests)
- Concern about other tenants impacting performance ("noisy neighbor")

Notes from the call
- You currently run inference on a mix of internal model infra + managed APIs; moving more real-time recommendations to an external inference layer to save ops overhead.
- Lina: primary ask is clear isolation for compliance and predictable tail latency.
- Samir: curious about performance isolation in our Hosted tier and what we'd get with Dedicated vs Private.

Attachments: I've attached a short deployment-mode matrix and our Dedicated overview PDF that calls out isolation, noise mitigation, and SLO guarantees.

Proposed next steps
1) Quick technical deep-dive with our solutions engineer (Priyom / Dev) to review your traffic profile and SLOs — 30 min.
2) If Dedicated looks like the right fit, we'll produce an initial capacity proposal with throughput & cost estimates.
3) If you need full network isolation/compliance we can scope Private (VPC or on-prem) and surface timeline/installation checklist.

Are you available for a 30-min follow-up on Thursday (3/25) or Friday (3/26)? If you prefer, Priyom can also run a short isolation/latency demo showing noisy-neighbor behavior and how our Dedicated pools handle bursty tenants.

Thanks,
Marissa
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198

Subject: Re: Deployment mode follow-up — hosted vs dedicated vs private (noisy neighbor concerns)

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Isolation: our security team requires logical separation of workloads that handle PII from general workloads. Full physical isolation (dedicated) is preferred but we can consider strict tenancy rules if Hosted gives equivalent guarantees.
- Noisy neighbor: the main risk we saw in other vendors was degraded p95/p99 during peaks when other tenants burst. We need to understand what isolation level you provide for Dedicated pools (e.g., dedicated GPU slices, preempt protection, CPU/RAM limits per tenant).
- SLO enforcement: we need an ops SLA for tail latency and capacity pre-warm guidance for flash sales.

We'd like the follow-up demo. Thursday 3/25 at 10am PT works for Lina and me.

Also: can you share any customer examples or anonymized benchmarks showing p95/p99 behavior under multi-tenant bursts? That would help get internal buy-in.

Best,
Samir
Head of ML Platform | Acme Retail
samir.khan@acme-retail.com

Hi Samir — looking forward to the call Thursday. A few quick notes so we can tailor the demo: 

- Can you share (or confirm) typical qps and peak qps for recommendation/generation endpoints, and the typical distribution of sequence lengths? This helps us size batchers and quantization profiles.
- Do you expect tail-latency sensitive traffic to be colocated with best-effort batch workloads? If so, Dedicated is typically the best fit. For Hosted we provide request-level QoS and auto-fallbacks, but isolation is ultimately limited by shared physical resources.
- For Dedicated pools we offer: dedicated GPU assignments (no shared GPU across customers), configurable preemption protection, and per-tenant resource reservations for CPU/RAM + network egress shaping. We'll demo a synthetic noisy-neighbor burst to show p95/p99 delta.

I'll prepare a short synthetic showing 3 scenarios: Hosted (shared), Dedicated (isolated pool), Private (VPC + on-prem if you want full network isolation).

Thanks — Priyom
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
